newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hogs seen steady-off $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hogs seen steady-off $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Friday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower amid continued pressure from large marketings, livestock dealers said.
The top plant price in Iowa and southern Minnesota has fallen $4.00 this week to $55.00 in the face of ample hog and pork supplies and pinched packer operating margins, they said.
Packers' margins have been tightened recently despite their ability to buy hogs at lower prices, because wholesale pork prices also have come under pressure.
Top Iowa/southern Minnesota prices for hogs delivered to plants Friday were seen at $54.00 to $54.50, sources said.
Illinois top prices at the plant could range from $53.00 to $54.00 and Indiana/Ohio top plant prices could range from $53.00 to $53.50, sources in those areas said.

Brisk hog marketings were reflected in lower pork prices at midday despite active sales Wednesday that resulted in over 175 total loads sold, sources said. Any day that sees 90 loads sold is considered an active one, some sources noted.
Midday pork prices were weak in slow trading, with heavy hams down $1.00 to $2.00 per cwt and bellies down mostly $1.00 to $2.00 on 23 loads of pork sold, according to USDA.

Hog runs were expected to be heavy again Friday as rainfall in parts of the western Corn Belt forces farmers to abandon fieldwork and concentrate on marketing hogs held back by harvesting, the sources said.
